# Gnobbi vendored gpui

- Version: 0.2.2 (Apache-2.0).
- Official archive: https://static.crates.io/crates/gpui/gpui-0.2.2.crate
- Archive SHA-256: `979b45cfa6ec723b6f42330915a1b3769b930d02b2d505f9697f8ca602bee707`.
- Upstream source file modified: `src/platform/linux/wayland/client.rs`. `wl_keyboard::Event::Modifiers` and `Key` unwrapped `keymap_state`, which stays `None` until a `keymap` event arrives; a compositor (sway after `wtype`) may send `modifiers` first, which panicked at startup. Both events are now ignored while no keymap is known, and the `Modifiers` arm no longer unwraps at all (two locals, as in the upstream PR).
- Upstream source file modified: `src/platform/linux/x11/client.rs`. Enables XKB DetectableAutoRepeat at startup: without it the X server turns every key repeat into a KeyRelease+KeyPress pair, and gpui only hides the release when both land in one poll batch, so a held Space/Enter reached apps as a real release (intermittent double activation, test `theme_unread_require_completed_current_keyboard_gestures`). Not yet proposed upstream; `is_held` stays `false` on X11.
- Upstream source file modified: `src/platform/linux/text_system.rs`, plus two Linux dependencies in `Cargo.toml` (`icu_properties` 2.3.0, `unicode-segmentation` 1.13; both already in Cargo.lock). `layout_line` splits each font run at grapheme clusters that are emoji (contain U+FE0F or start with an Emoji_Presentation character: faces, flags, ZWJ and skin-tone sequences, keycaps) and gives them the "Noto Color Emoji" family registered by the app (`crates/matrix-desktop/src/emoji_font.rs`). Without it a text font with its own monochrome glyph for U+1F600 (DejaVu Sans) wins over the colour fallback; upstream has no fallback list on Linux (`TODO: Remove this when Linux have implemented setting fallbacks`). No-op when the family is not registered. Test: `emoji_font::tests::every_emoji_cluster_is_one_noto_glyph` (fails without the patch).
- Upstream source file modified: `src/elements/text.rs`. The measure callback cached the first text size whenever the text does not wrap (`white_space: nowrap`), ignoring `truncate_width`; taffy measures a `flex_1` + `truncate()` child first with indefinite width, so the full-width size was cached and the later definite-width pass never truncated: the name was clipped without «…». `TextLayoutInner` now stores `truncate_width` and the cache is reused only when it matches. Not yet proposed upstream. Check: `the gui-list-stamp-shot script` (long group name ends with «…»).
- Upstream source file modified: `src/elements/text.rs` (second hunk). The measure callback owned `runs` and `truncate_line` shortened it in place; taffy measures the same text several times per frame, so a later measure that truncates elsewhere or not at all shaped the full text with runs cut at the previous truncation plus the ellipsis length: on macOS `layout_line` slices `&text[ix..][..run.len]` and panicked (not a char boundary, SIGABRT in the display link). Each measure now works on a copy of the original runs. Not yet proposed upstream. Check: probe row `flex_1().min_w_0().truncate()` with accented/emoji/CJK text at many widths on macOS.
- Upstream source file modified: `src/platform/windows/window.rs`; added `src/platform/windows/work_area.rs`. Fit initial window placement to the monitor work area, excluding popups. Remove these changes when a gpui release supports work-area-aware initial placement.
- Upstream source files modified: `src/platform/linux/wayland/client.rs`, `serial.rs`. `write_to_clipboard`/`write_to_primary` passed the last *key press* serial to `set_selection`; after a copy in another app a pointer click (button serial newer than the last key) was ignored by the compositor until a key was pressed. They now use `SerialTracker::latest_input()` (newer of key/button serial, wraparound-safe). Not yet proposed upstream. Test: `serial::tests` in the vendored crate; live check: wl-copy elsewhere, click a copy icon, wl-paste.
- Upstream source files modified: `src/platform.rs`, `src/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`, `client.rs`. New `Window::hide_window` (`PlatformWindow::hide`, default = minimize). `minimize` is `xdg_toplevel.set_minimized`, which sway and Hyprland ignore, so a close-to-tray window never left the screen. On Wayland `hide` attaches a null buffer and swaps the xdg_surface/xdg_toplevel for fresh ones (a compositor only sends a new configure to a new role); `activate_window` then does the initial commit and the first configure forces a paint. Frame callbacks: one outstanding at most (`frame_requested`), none are served while unmapped. Not yet proposed upstream. Test: `tests/gui/close-tray-wl.sh` (sway headless + waybar tray).
- Upstream: issues zed-industries/zed#64660 and #64959; fix PR zed-industries/zed#64970 (open on 2026-10-30).
- Removal (wayland/x11 fixes): drop those two hunks, `../gpui-0.2.2.patch` and the `[patch.crates-io]` entry once that PR is merged and released in a gpui version we bump to.
- Regression test: `crates/matrix-desktop/tests/wayland_keymap_order.rs` (fake compositor).
- `../gpui-0.2.2.patch` is generated using `diff -ruN` from the extracted official archive to this directory, excluding the added distribution file `GNOBBI-PATCH.md`. All other upstream files remain byte-identical.
